newsitem.title: USA: GM declines comment on Hughes sale reports.
newsitem.headline: GM declines comment on Hughes sale reports.

text.p: General Motors Corp. declined comment on published reports Thursday that it will sell its Hughes Electronics defence operations to Raytheon Corp. in a deal worth $9.5 billion.
However, a source familiar with the situation said an announcement regarding Hughes might be made later in the day Thursday.
The Wall Street Journal, citing unidentified sources, reported that GM's board of directors was meeting in New York Thursday and was expected to approve the deal.
The Boston Globe, Boston Herald and Defence Daily, an industry trade publication, also reported that Raytheon was the winner of a heated bidding war for Hughes with Northrop Grumman Corp.
A Raytheon-Hughes merger would likely create the nation's third largest defence contractor, behind the combination of Boeing Co. and McDonnell Douglas Corp., and Lockheed Martin Corp.
The combined company would control more than 80 percent of the U.S. missile business, according to defence industry analysts.
Hughes' defence operations, based in Los Angeles, produce missiles such as the Tomahawk cruise missile, radar systems and other defence electronics systems.

Earlier Thursday, GM announced that it is relocating Hughes' armoured vehicle turret manufacturing operations to London, Ontario -- a step viewed as part of a reorganization of Hughes' remaining assets.
The turret business will be folded into GM's Electro-Motive Division, which builds locomotives and armoured military vehicles.

GM is expected to move Hughes' automotive electronics business back into its Delphi Automotive Systems parts unit. GM combined the Delco Electronics business with Hughes after it purchsed Hughes in 1985 for about $5 billion.
The future operating structure of Hughes' lucrative satellite and communications business, which include the fast-growing DirecTV satellite broadcasting service, was still unclear.

Raytheon, based in Lexington, Mass., also makes missiles, including the Patriot air defence missile, radar and air-traffic control and communications systems. Raytheon also produces Amana appliances and Beech aircraft.
